attribution: proofbundle (6.6.1 holder-binding vector: an issuer-signed SD-JWT whose cnf.jwk is an EC P-256 key, presented with NO Key Binding JWT; everything else about the bundle verifies)
rationale: The issuer bound the credential to a holder key (RFC 7800 cnf), here an EC P-256 jwk. proofbundle reads an OKP/Ed25519 cnf.jwk only, so it cannot check possession of this key. A cnf that is present asks for proof of possession whether or not the verifier can read it: the presentation carries no Key Binding JWT, so verify MUST reject it (exit 1, sd-jwt-key-binding=False), not read the unreadable cnf as no binding. Until 6.6.0 proofbundle verify accepted this bundle (exit 0) while pb_verify_rs verify-bundle rejected it (exit 1): the two verifiers disagreed, and no vector of this corpus carried a cnf of another key type. The bundle signature, the inclusion proof and the issuer signature all verify, and the SD-JWT carries no receipt.root_b64 commitment, so the verdict isolates the holder-binding rule.
